lines.text: Abortion and euthanasia.
Abortion [Abortus] means that a pregnant woman has her child removed/terminated [weghalen].
That is allowed in the Netherlands until the woman is 24 weeks pregnant.
Euthanasia [Euthanasie] means "good death": people who are very ill, are in a lot of pain and will not get better can get help from a doctor to die [sterven] earlier.
That is only possible if someone really wants it themselves, and there are strict conditions [voorwaarden].
Abortion and euthanasia are regulated in Dutch law [wet].
Being a donor after your death.
After your death [overlijden], other people can receive your organs [organen]; that is called organ donation [orgaandonatie].
Organ donation is not compulsory [verplicht].

You register your choice in the donor register [donorregister], on the internet or with a paper form: yes, I want to become a donor; no, I do not want to be a donor; my partner or family decides; or I want to designate [aanwijzen] one person who decides.
If you register nothing?
Then the register says "no objection" [Geen bezwaar] — then after your death they may give your organs to sick people.
That is what the law says.
Making your own choices.
All adults in the Netherlands may decide about their own body themselves.
Taking medicines, physical examination or a vaccination [vaccinatie] — that only happens if you agree yourself.
Kissing or sex is also only allowed by law if you really want it yourself.
It is punishable/a criminal offence [strafbaar] if someone forces [dwingt] you to do something you do not want.
Forbidden in the Netherlands, and therefore punishable:
Rape [Verkrachting]: forcing someone to have sex.
Also within a marriage [huwelijk] someone may not force their partner.
Sex between an adult and someone under sixteen years old, even if that person gives consent themselves.
Honour killing [Eerwraak]: a girl or woman is murdered because she has had sex without being married.
Eerwraak is murder [moord] and is forbidden.
Circumcision [Besnijdenis] of girls and women is forbidden.
Circumcision of boys and men is not forbidden.
Violence [Geweld] (hurting someone, for example with a weapon or knife) is forbidden; also at home — that is called domestic violence [huiselijk geweld].
Having weapons is forbidden; only the police may have a weapon.
Abuse/assault [Mishandeling]: causing someone a lot of pain, for example hitting.
Also in a relationship [relatie] you may not hurt your partner.
